previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pancreatitis, portal hypertension, esophageal varices, and asthma was admitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and blood-streaked emesis following a relapse in alcohol use. He had been consuming two pints of brandy daily for two weeks and reported drinking to alleviate pain and withdrawal symptoms, including tremors and visual hallucinations. Initial labs showed elevated alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, and hypernatremia, with a positive serum ethanol level. Imaging confirmed cirrhosis with portal hypertension and splenomegaly. He was treated for presumed alcoholic hepatitis and chronic pancreatitis with pain control, IV fluids, and symptom management. Alcohol withdrawal was monitored with CIWA, and he received Ativan as needed. Asthma was managed with a prednisone taper and inhalers. His condition improved, with stable vital signs, improved labs, and reduced pain. He was discharged home on his baseline medications, including nadolol, spironolactone, omeprazole, and lactulose, with a short prednisone course and follow-up arranged with primary care and addiction services.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male with history of alcohol abuse, pancreatitis, 
cirrhosis, asthma who was recently admitted with abdominal pain 
and elevated liver function tests concerning for acute flare of 
pancreatitis vs. alcoholic hepatitis presented again with 
worsening abdominal discomfort and inability to tolerate 
anything by mouth.

ACTIVE ISSUES
-------------
# Abdominal pain: presented with elevated liver enzymes and 
elevated total bilirubin with a normal lipase. This injury is 
consistent with alcoholic hepatitis versus chronic pancreatitis. 
 A right upper quadrant ultrasound was negative for acute 
cholecystitis.  While his abdominal pain was worse, his diet was 
held and he was given intravenous fluids and intravenous pain 
medications. As his pain improved, his diet was advanced slowly 
and he was switched to oral pain medications. His liver enzymes 
(bilirubin, AST, ALT) were trending down at the time of 
discharge although his alkaline phosphatase remained elevated.  
He will follow up with his PCP following discharge.

# Cirrhosis: most likely from extensive history of heavy alcohol 
use, although the patient is rather young. He has had an 
extensive workup in past - hepatitis B and C serologies are 
negative, as are alpha antitrypsin, ceruloplasmin, and 
schistosoma antibodies.  Also, AMA is negative.  Prior iron 
studies not consistent with hemochromatosis.  He has been noted 
to have multiple perigastric and perisplenic varices consistent 
with portal hypertension on previous imaging. EGD in ___ 
negative for esophageal varices. Synthetic function fairly 
normal with the exception of slightly low platelets. His liver 
disease is compensated at this time. No evidence of hepatic 
encephalopathy, ascites, GI bleed, jaundice at this time. He was 
continued on lactulose, nadolol, and aldactone. He will follow 
up in the liver clinic at ___.

# Alcohol abuse: has history of withdrawal on prior admissions 
where he experienced tactile hallucinations, anxiety, and 
tremulousness. He has history of withdrawal seizures.  He was 
placed on withdrawal precautions with lorazepam as needed for 
symptoms.  He did not require any benzodiazepines during his 
admission.  Social work was consulted for assistance in helping 
Mr. ___ stay sober. 

# Anion gap metabolic acidosis: likely multifactorial from 
lactic acidosis, alcohol, and starvation ketosis (poor intake 
over the past few days per the patient's history).  This 
improved and resolved with fluids. 

# Asthma: completed recent steroid taper on his last admission. 
He was continued on his home medications Advair, montelukast, 
cetirizine and albuterol nebulizer treatments as needed.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Right upper quadrant pain, history of hepatitis.  Question
cholestatic process, cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, portal vein
thrombosis.

COMPARISON:  Prior abdominal ultrasound from ___ and ___.

FINDINGS:

The liver demonstrates diffuse echogenicity consistent with fatty
infiltration.  There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The common bile duct
measures 4 mm.  The gallbladder is normal without evidence of stones or
gallbladder wall thickening.  Visualized portions of the pancreas are
unremarkable without evidence of focal lesions or pancreatic duct dilatation. 
The spleen is enlarged measuring 14.3 cm.  Representative images of the right
kidney are normal.  There is no ascites. 

DOPPLER COLOR FLOW AND SPECTRAL WAVEFORM ANALYSIS: Limited evaluation due to
respiratory artifact. The main, left and right portal veins, including the
anterior and posterior branches are patent. There is redemonstration of
reversal of flow in the main and right portal veins. The left portal vein
demonstrates adequate directionality of flow.  The main hepatic artery
presents a normal waveform.  The right, middle and left hepatic veins are
patent.  The IVC is within normal limits.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Echogenic liver consistent with fatty deposition.  Other forms of liver
disease and more advanced liver disease including significant hepatic fibrosis
or cirrhosis cannot be excluded on this study. 

2.  Redemonstration of reversal of flow in the main and right portal veins. 
Patent hepatic vasculature. 

3.  No evidence of acute cholecystitis.  

4.  Splenomegaly.
